column1: OTIS COMMERCIAL CLEANING — LEAD TRACKER
Built by Golden Thread Solutions · September 2026 · English-only v2
THE GOAL: LONG-TERM CONTRACTS
Everything in this tracker exists to win recurring contracts. Nothing else is the finish line.
The problem is that you cannot win a contract cold. Almost every business already has a cleaner,
so a contract means replacing someone — and that only happens when they have a reason.
So there are two ways IN, and both of them lead to the same place:
ROUTE 1 — THE ONE-OFF JOB
Strip and wax, post-construction, deep clean, event clean. Work their current cleaner does not do.
Nobody gets replaced. You get inside the building and they watch you work.
→ Then you ask about the contract.
ROUTE 2 — THE BACKUP LIST
'Put us on your list for when your cleaner doesn't turn up.' No budget, no decision, no risk.
The easiest yes in this business. You get called the moment a competitor fails.
→ Fill-in jobs are where contracts come from.
THE DESTINATION — THE CONTRACT
Track it deliberately in the Contract stage column. A one-off job that never becomes a
contract conversation is a job you did, not a client you won.
HOW THIS WORKS
Five tabs. You work in Leads. Everything else supports it.

This page.
2. Compliance pack
What must be true before a quote can close. Fill in ONCE. A quote that dies three weeks in
because a certificate was missing is the most avoidable loss there is.
3. Where to look
Where leads come from, best first. Work down. Do not skip to the bottom.
4. Leads
The working tab. Colour-coded by who fills each column — see the legend on that tab.
5. Pipeline
Counts everything automatically. Do not type in it.
COLOUR CODE ON THE LEADS TAB
BLUE   — the Otis Lead Sourcing skill fills these for you.
AMBER  — YOU fill these by hand as the work happens. These are the ones to look for.
GREY   — calculates itself. Never type in these.
THE RULES
•  Offer a WALKTHROUGH, not a pitch.
•  Send the proposal FAST. Slow proposals lose more deals than high prices do.
•  Name a supervisor in every proposal. 'No named supervisor' is a known deal-killer.
•  Fill in Source URL and Date collected on EVERY row. Legal record under CASL, and the
burden of proof is on the sender. No exceptions.
•  Never quote a price before a walkthrough.
•  Follow up more than feels comfortable. Most people do not reply first time.
•  Every won job asks one question afterwards: can this become a contract?
WHAT THEY ARE ACTUALLY BUYING
Not clean premises. Fewer complaints, and one less problem to manage.
